stories.notes: Acceptance criteria are empty — openspec must elaborate AC and add technical depth around ContentStack Live Preview SDK integration (draft entry preview, CMS-side rendering, content-type scoping). Speckit then hardens testability criteria, covers the protected-page/content limitation edge case, and flags security gaps around unauthorized preview access. No prd.json or provider policy files were found in the repository, so no hand-curation skip or provider restriction applies. No upstream dependencies to gate on.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — the codebase has zero Live Preview support today. The Stack options lack live_preview config, interfaces carry no draft flag, and the catch-all page has no preview-mode detection. All attachment points are in the data-fetching and page-rendering pipeline. Verification criteria stop at our boundary: they assume the Contentstack SDK client is mocked to signal preview state, never asserting real contentstack.io behaviour.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so all 20 criteria are new. Key findings from codebase analysis: (1) The app uses SSG (getStaticProps/getStaticPaths) with filesystem caching — Live Preview requires a shift to SSR or ISR with preview-mode detection in getStaticProps, which AC-1 and AC-12 implicitly require. (2) The Stack in contentstack.ts is initialized without live_preview config — AC-8 addresses this. (3) Zero existing preview-related code was found (search confirmed no matches for live_preview, livePreview, preview_token, etc.). (4) The catch-all page reads from FS cache and never checks context.preview — AC-1 and AC-2 cover the branching. (5) Three codelines have different file sets (partnersPromotionsService.ts and applyMiddlewares.ts absent in metrolinx; ContentstackLinksGroup absent in metrolinx) — AC-17 addresses cross-codeline consistency. (6) The story explicitly states protected pages cannot be previewed — AC-7 captures this. (7) Security consideration: the current Stack options expose api_key and delivery_token server-side only; Live Preview SDK requires a client-side app_key which must not leak the delivery_token — AC-16 addresses this. (8) Performance guard added as AC-15 because adding SSR branching to an SSG pipeline could introduce latency. (9) Accessibility AC-20 ensures preview instrumentation (data attributes, script tags) does not break a11y. File contents were read in full for contentstack.ts, the catch-all page, pageService.ts, and interfaces — criteria are grounded in actual code patterns.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Brownfield ticket with empty acceptanceCriteria (expected per redaction policy) and 5 verificationCriteria that are all observable page-surface checks. Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: OpenSpec correctly identified this as a novel capability (zero existing Live Preview support) and mapped attachment points in the data-fetch/render pipeline; Speckit performed deep codebase analysis covering SSG→SSR/ISR implications, security (client-side app_key must not leak delivery_token), cross-codeline file-set differences, and added performance/a11y guardrails. The guardVocabulary blacklist/whitelist shows careful curation separating observable surface terms from internal mechanism terms. All 8 manifest paths EXIST for the primary gotransit codeline — no missing_manifest_path. The fixSiteAnalysis identifies 5 fix sites all within declared files, grounded in actual code patterns (Stack options lacking live_preview config, getPageContent as the central fetcher, catch-all page with no preview detection, partnersPromotionsService bypassing centralized factory, interfaces needing includeDraft). Plan alignment is genuine: detectivePlan expected centralized Contentstack init in src/services, Pages Router, and no existing live_preview config — all confirmed by fixSiteAnalysis with shared terms (contentstack, etc.). No pivot, no explanation gap. Advisory concerns: (1) cross-codeline gaps — metrolinx is missing 3 of 8 declared paths (partnersPromotionsService.ts, ContentstackLinksGroup/content.mock.ts, applyMiddlewares.ts) and upexpress is missing partnersPromotionsService.ts, yet the ticket title targets [GO, UP, MX]; implementer must handle per-codeline differences. (2) fixSiteAnalysis for partnersPromotionsService.ts references stationService.ts, blogService.ts, and userAccountService.ts as additional files needing the same draft-inclusion refactor, but these are not in the declared file set — an implementer may miss them. Neither concern blocks implementation on the primary codeline.
